prompt: Write a recorded statement transcript (about 250 words) between an insurance adjuster (lines start with 'Q:') and the claimant (lines start with 'A:'). The claimant was the driver in a rear-end collision in Sugar Land, Texas, and has back strain. No names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1416; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Thanks for taking the time to speak with me today. This call is being recorded for claim file purposes. Can you confirm you're comfortable continuing?

A: Yes, that's fine.

Q: Great. Can you walk me through what happened on the day of the accident?

A: I was stopped at a red light on a main road in Sugar Land, in the right lane. Traffic had been moving slowly. The next thing I knew, I felt a hard jolt from behind and my head snapped back against the headrest.

Q: Did you see the vehicle coming before the impact?

A: No. I was looking ahead at the light. I heard tires and then the impact.

Q: Were you able to get out of your car afterward?

A: Yes, but I felt stiff. Within an hour my lower back was really tight and sore, and by that evening it was shooting pain down my left leg.

Q: Did you seek medical attention?

A: I went to an urgent care clinic the next morning. They took x-rays, said there was no fracture, and diagnosed a back strain. They gave me muscle relaxers and told me to rest and do stretching.

Q: Are you still having symptoms?

A: Yes. I still get stiffness when I sit for long periods, and I've had to cut back on lifting at work. I have a follow-up with my primary care doctor next week.

Q: Did you have any pain or problems with your back before this accident?

A: I had some occasional stiffness after long shifts, but nothing that stopped me from working or needed treatment.

Q: Is there anything else you'd like to add?

A: Just that I'm trying to get back to normal and I want the claim handled fairly.

Q: Thank you. We'll be in touch with next steps. This concludes the recorded statement.
